codex-vscode-health: full description

What it is
codex-vscode-health is a health gate for the Codex VS Code extension's renderer_ready_timeout failures on remote hosts. It is a single bash script, bin/vscode-health.sh, plus three docs (DIAGNOSIS, PREVENTION, RUNBOOK). It is MIT licensed by MHJoy99 and labelled experimental (the shellcheck badge is still TODO). It is not affiliated with OpenAI or Microsoft.

The problem
The Codex sidebar in VS Code fails to render, but the codex app-server backend is healthy. The client log shows:
  [CodexWebviewProvider] Webview renderer did not become ready after 30000ms
  reason=renderer_ready_timeout
while the server log shows:
  codex app-server: Initialize received id=1
The renderer budget is a fixed 30 seconds. In the documented incident (2026-09-16, VS Code 1.132.0, 6 vCPU, 7.8G RAM host) server-side memory and load pressure delayed extension-host activation past that budget: load 7.2, about 1.8G memory available, 3.6G swap used, 2 extensionHost processes (about 1.5G), 2 "kilo serve" processes (about 1.4G), about 20 php-fpm processes, ~/.codex at 459M with logs_2.sqlite at 136M, disk at 84%, several AI extensions all activating on onStartupFinished, and Codex extension version drift (26.5908 on disk versus 26.908 in the log). The Codex CLI ("codex" in a terminal) keeps working when the webview does not.

What the script checks
1. Memory and swap (free -m): warn if available memory < 2500M, critical if < 1500M, warn if swap used > 3000M.
2. CPU load (/proc/loadavg, 1 minute): warn if > nproc, critical if > 1.5 x nproc.
3. Disk usage of /: warn at 80% or more, critical at 90% or more.
4. Duplicate "kilo serve --port 0" processes: warn if more than one.
5. extensionHost process count: warn if more than one (use Developer: Reload Window, do not pkill).
6. ~/.codex bloat: warn if the directory is > 400M or logs_2.sqlite is > 100M; also warns if Codex.log contains stale_rollout_path_retained.
7. Codex extension installs (openai.chatgpt-* under ~/.vscode-server/extensions): warn if there are none or more than one.
8. AI extension pile-up: tracks five extensions (kilocode.kilo-code, qwenlm.qwen-code-vscode-ide-companion, rooveterinaryinc.roo-cline, google.google-antigravity, openai.chatgpt); warn if more than three are installed.
9. VS Code log sets older than 14 days in ~/.vscode-server/data/logs.
Memory, load and disk can be critical; the others only warn.

Exit codes
0 healthy, 1 warning, 2 critical. On critical, the script also prints client-side steps: Developer: Reload With Extensions Disabled and enable only Codex, update the Codex extension and match local and remote VS Code versions, clear %APPDATA%\Code\Cache and GPUCache and try --disable-gpu, and fall back to the codex CLI.

Usage
  git clone https://github.com/MHJoy99/codex-vscode-health.git
  cd codex-vscode-health
  chmod +x bin/vscode-health.sh
  bin/vscode-health.sh          # read-only check, safe in cron/SSH
  bin/vscode-health.sh --fix    # check + safe fixes only
Requirements: bash with coreutils and procps (the optional VACUUM path uses sqlite3). It reads ~/.vscode-server and ~/.codex on the remote host.

What --fix does (and only this)
- Kills older duplicate "kilo serve --port 0" processes, keeping the newest.
- Prunes ~/.vscode-server/data/logs/20* sets older than 14 days.
- Backs up and runs VACUUM on ~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite, only when app-server is stopped.
It never touches php-fpm, mysql, nginx, reverb, queue workers, prod htdocs, the newest kilo serve, extensionHost, or Codex session rows. Never run --fix unattended; in cron use check-only mode, for example:
  */15 * * * * /root/codex-vscode-health/bin/vscode-health.sh >> ~/.codex/health.log 2>&1

Runbook (docs/RUNBOOK.md), follow in order and stop at the first fix
1. Confirm the backend is healthy (Initialize received id=1 plus renderer_ready_timeout in Codex.log).
2. Run bin/vscode-health.sh and read the exit code.
3. Run bin/vscode-health.sh --fix.
4. Developer: Reload Window; then Reload With Extensions Disabled and enable only Codex.
5. Reinstall the Codex extension on version drift (exactly one openai.chatgpt-* install).
6. VACUUM ~/.codex/logs_2.sqlite with a backup, only while app-server is stopped.
7. Clear %APPDATA%\Code\Cache and GPUCache on the Windows client; try code --disable-gpu.

Limits and honesty
Thresholds are tuned from one incident on one host (6 vCPU, 7.8G RAM); the project is experimental. Contribution rules: thresholds must cite measured incident data, no destructive fixes, run shellcheck and bash -n before a PR. When reporting a case, scrub Codex.log first and never paste tokens or ~/.codex/auth.json.
